data.value: Your pay, plus the contributions the company pays for you

data.name: NextCompanyPaysNote
data.value: The contributions are what the next €1,000 adds to those the company pays for you, on top of it: the other parts add up to €1,000, and all of them to what it costs the company, so the shares go over 100% together.

data.name: StatementHint
data.value: Twelve equal months of pay, each withheld on by the administration's key formula with the rules in force when it is paid; the net paid is the gross less the withholding. A real payslip may differ by a cent where its software rounds.

data.name: BalanceTitle
data.value: Your year's balance on the assessment

data.name: BalanceHint
data.value: What your tax return leaves once the withholding and your advance payments are set against the final tax.

data.name: Withheld_Derived
data.value: Withheld on your pay, as the pay slip above derives it

data.name: Withheld_Given
data.value: Withheld on your pay, as you entered it

data.name: FinalTax_WithRent
data.value: Final tax on your pay and the rent taxed with it

data.name: NextRentNote
data.value: Your home office rent is taxed with your pay, so these are the year's taxes: the next €1,000 of pay also raises the tax on the rent, which is in its parts.

data.name: FinalTaxOnRoyalty
data.value: of which on your copyright royalty within its limits

data.name: WithheldOnRoyalty
data.value: Withheld by the company on your copyright royalty

data.name: NextFollowingRoyaltyNote
data.value: The next 1,000 holds your copyright royalty as it is, though it follows your pay: it leaves out the royalty's own rise beside it and that rise's tax apart. The split's curve weighs both.

data.name: NextRoyaltyNote
data.value: The next 1,000 holds your copyright royalty's part beyond its limits as it is, though 30% of the pay moves that limit: the split's curve weighs it.

data.name: FinalTax_WithRoyalty
data.value: Final tax on your pay and your copyright royalty

data.name: FinalTax_WithRentAndRoyalty
data.value: Final tax on your pay, the rent taxed with it and your copyright royalty
